task_3_formal_explanation.label: CLAUDE_HAND_PROOF -- general theory, independent of whether the defect exists here
steps: 1. Pure rotation (SIGMA) does not preserve E-orbit membership in general -- the mechanism behind r2_wrong_source_orbit existing at all.
2. ORBIT_PHASE[macro_entry_state.p] and ORBIT_PHASE[edge.run.state.p] are, in general, different orbits whenever the rotation-run length ell>0; they coincide only in the degenerate case ell=0.

3. extend()'s own new_orbit=(orbit_masks[q]==0) classification (deciding R vs Z3) is evaluated at edge.run.state, the state the joint actually fires from -- the state whose orbit-openness decided the R-classification in the first place.

4. Using a different state's orbit for the recognizer's same-component test would compute forest membership for an orbit unrelated to why the edge was classified R in the first place -- an internal inconsistency between classifier and recognizer, not a stricter or looser version of the same question.
5. Therefore the two are not interchangeable for any ell>0, and ell>0 is not rare: all 49,440 R2 candidates in the analyzed run have ell=5 exactly (re-cited from two rounds ago, not re-derived).
